headline: TRUMP COPPER TARIFF RESTRUCTURE LIVE TODAY — SECTION 232 SLAPS 50% ON MOST COPPER AS JUNE 30 REFINED REVIEW TICKS DOWN
snippet: Section 232 tariff restructuring on aluminum, steel, and copper took effect June 8, 2026, applying a 50% rate to most copper articles and 25% to select derivatives under a White House proclamation signed June 1. The US-origin metal threshold was also lowered from 95% to 85%. The changes arrive alongside a separate June 30 Commerce Department assessment that could add a 15% refined copper tariff from January 2027, rising to 30% from January 2028.

headline: TRAFIGURA YANKS 51,000+ TONNES FROM LME WAREHOUSES — COMEX PREMIUM HITS $500/T AS TRADERS FRONT-RUN JUNE 30 TARIFF CALL
snippet: Trafigura pulled over 51,000 tonnes of copper from London Metal Exchange warehouses ahead of the US Commerce Department's June 30 refined copper tariff review, with total LME cancelled warrants exceeding 50,000 tonnes in a single session — a magnitude rarely seen in over a decade. COMEX front-month copper now commands more than $500 per tonne above LME spot, and the March 2027 forward premium has approached $1,000/t, as producers and traders accelerate shipments into the US to beat potential 15% refined duties beginning January 2027.

headline: KACHIN STATE BATTLEFIELD SUPPLIES HALF THE WORLD'S HEAVY RARE EARTHS — AND THE OFFENSIVE IS ADVANCING
snippet: Myanmar's Kachin State — where the Kachin Independence Army has held operational control over the Chipwi and Pangwa extraction districts — produces roughly 70% of China's heavy rare earth feedstock, including the dysprosium and terbium essential for high-performance NdFeB magnets in EV motors and wind turbines. With intensified military operations ongoing through mid-2026 and no commercially viable substitutes for these elements, analysts say physical access has replaced pricing as the binding market constraint. The disruption is distinct from China's own export-licence controls and represents an upstream supply-chain risk that downstream magnet makers cannot hedge.

headline: SAXO BANK: COPPER FACES 'TARIFF ROULETTE' — BUT SHANGHAI INVENTORY LOWS AND STRUCTURAL DEFICIT KEEP THE BULL CASE INTACT
snippet: Saxo Bank commodities strategist Ole Hansen argues that while the June 30 Commerce Department decision creates binary pricing risk for copper, the physical market remains genuinely tight: Shanghai Futures Exchange inventories fell to yearly lows last week on resilient Chinese buying, LME warehouse cancellations signal continued withdrawals, and J.P. Morgan's base-case structural deficit stands at 330,000 tonnes for 2026. Any tariff-driven demand disruption may prove shorter-lived than the supply constraints building through a decade of underinvestment.

headline: GDX DOWN 27% FROM MARCH RECORD — GOLD MINERS STUCK IN NEUTRAL EVEN AS BULLION HOLDS ABOVE $4,300
snippet: VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) sits at $85.60 — 26.9% below its March 2026 record of $117.17 — while GDXJ is at $113.99, off 27.6% from its $157.49 peak, even though COMEX gold futures are only 3.5% higher year-to-date. The underperformance reverses the explosive 2025 leverage (GDX +152.9%, GDXJ +166.2%) and signals reduced speculative interest in mining equities during the current consolidation. Analysts are split: either the dislocation is a setup for another leg higher once gold stabilises, or the sector is pricing in a structural derating as costs and capex rise faster than metals prices.

headline: SELKIRK COPPER WRAPS 52,288m PHASE 1 AT MINTO — HIGH-GRADE CU-AU-AG AT FIVE TARGETS, PHASE 2 ALREADY 14,000m IN
snippet: Selkirk Copper (TSXV: SCMI) completed its 52,288-metre Phase 1 drill program at the historic Minto copper-gold-silver mine in Yukon, confirming high-grade mineralization at all five primary target areas, including a new 202 Lens hit of 3.56% Cu, 2.34 g/t Au, and 21.42 g/t Ag over 3.7 metres. An updated mineral resource estimate is expected in June 2026. The 50,000-metre Phase 2 program was initiated in May and has already turned 14,000 metres in its first month, with four rigs averaging 120 metres per day.

headline: YUKON METALS TURNS FIRST RIGS AT AZ AND BIRCH — 5,000m COPPER-GOLD CAMPAIGN KICKS OFF IN WHITEHORSE DISTRICT
snippet: Yukon Metals Corp. (CSE: YMC; OTCQB: YMMCF) has commenced a fully funded 5,000-metre diamond drill program at its AZ and Birch copper-gold properties in the Whitehorse Mining District. The program follows up on a 47-metre gold intercept from prior drilling and targets four geologically prioritised zones across both properties. Results are expected through Q3 2026.

headline: GOLD TESTS $4,336 SUPPORT AFTER JOBS-SHOCK WIPEOUT — ANALYSTS EYE DOUBLE-BOTTOM SETUP FOR $4,800 YEAR-END RECOVERY
snippet: Gold recovered to $4,336/oz on June 7 — up 0.13% — after the prior week's 4% rout triggered by the blowout May payrolls report. Technical analysts are flagging a double-bottom pattern at the $4,336–$4,370 demand zone with a change-of-character signal to the upside, while Commerzbank targets $4,800/oz by year-end and J.P. Morgan maintains a Q4 2026 target of $6,300. The emerging consensus: extreme speculative washout combined with intact structural demand (central bank buying, de-dollarisation, fiscal deterioration) creates an asymmetric risk/reward entry point ahead of the autumn-winter seasonal rally.

headline: URANIUM STOCKS OUTPERFORM DESPITE METALS SELLOFF — AI DATA CENTRES AND STRUCTURAL DEFICIT REWRITING THE THESIS
snippet: Uranium equities are holding up relative to broader metals names in June 2026, with spot prices near multi-year highs and long-term contract prices at their strongest since 2008. The investment case has been refreshed by surging electricity demand from AI data centres and clean-energy grid buildout — both requiring reliable nuclear baseload — layered on top of a chronic supply deficit driven by underinvestment since 2011. Cameco, Denison (whose Phoenix ISR project broke ground June 7), and NexGen continue to attract institutional attention, with utilities extending long-term contract coverage after the May Cameco Key Lake supply disruption.
